subject: Kestrel renewal — proposal to elevate support tier + latency SLOs (term & capacity)
messages:
From: Alicia Turner <alicia@kestrel.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Kestrel renewal capacity + SLA conversation

Connor —

Our renewal for Q4 is coming up (contract ends 10/31). After the performance incident in June we've had internal pressure to tighten latency guarantees and get a cleaner on-call handoff. We'd like to discuss:

- Moving to Redwood's Premium Support tier (24/7 oncall + 30 min P1 response).
- A 99.9th percentile tail latency SLO for production generation requests (current contract is best-effort).
- Reservation of an extra 20% baseline capacity for peak periods (we've seen sustained growth).

Can you send a proposal with: term length options, uplifted SLO wording, estimated cost delta, and any ramp credits you can offer? Procurement would prefer a single-year term if possible, but they're open to multi-year pricing.

Thanks — happy to take a short call next week.

Alicia Turner
Head of Platform, Kestrel AI
Alicia Turner | Kestrel AI

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Turner <alicia@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel renewal capacity + SLA conversation

Alicia —

Appreciate the context and the clear asks. I put together two options below and attached an SLA addendum + mutual action plan for procurement. High level:

Option A — Premium SLO (12 month)
- Premium Support (24/7 on-call, 30 min P1 acknowledge, 4 hour P1 mitigation target)
- Latency SLO: 99.9th percentile < 450ms for text-generation requests (applies to production routes)
- Dedicated buffer: +20% baseline reserved capacity (billed as committed RUs)
- Price delta: +18% over current committed run-rate
- Onboarding: 2-week ops onramp, capacity smoke-test (included)

Option B — Pilot then commit (12 month)
- 3 month pilot at Premium Support (same SLO) with no term change; post-pilot, convert to 12 month at +15% run-rate and 10% account credit applied against month 1
- Pilot includes one dedicated spike day and a joint runbook review

Attachments: SLA_Addendum_v2.pdf (language + credits), Kestrel_Mutual_Action_Plan_2027-08.xlsx (timeline + signatures).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm preferred option (A or B).
2) If A, procurement signs SLA addendum; we produce DocuSign for contract amendment.
3) If B, we spin up pilot and share acceptance criteria; Laura will own ops onramp.

If you're available I can do a 30m call on Monday 16th at 10am PT — Laura will join for onboarding details.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Turner <alicia@kestrel.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kestrel Procurement <procurement@kestrel.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel renewal capacity + SLA conversation

Connor — thanks for the fast turnaround and the two-shelf approach. Quick clarifying Qs after discussing with engineering and procurement:

- For the 99.9th < 450ms SLO, is that for both short and long-sequence generation? Our critical use-case has variable sequence lengths up to 1k tokens.
- Can you confirm what the penalty/credit model looks like if we miss the SLO (monthly credit, sliding scale)?
- For Option B pilot, we'd like the pilot to include a guaranteed two-week window of elevated concurrency to validate tail behavior.

Procurement's preference is Option B initially (pilot then commit) but they want the pilot outcomes codified and binding: acceptance criteria + a maximum conversion price.

If you can update the SLA addendum with sequence-length carveouts and explicit credit language, we can move quickly. We'll also need a draft Statement of Work (or contract amendment) for legal.

—Alicia

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Turner <alicia@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel renewal capacity + SLA conversation

Alicia —

Thanks — looping in Ben (Head of Platform Sales) for pricing approval and Laura for ops commitments.

Ben/Laura — summary and asks from Kestrel: Pilot-first approach (Option B), pilot must include a 2-week elevated concurrency window to exercise 1k-token flows, explicit SLO credit language for 99.9th < 450ms across the supported sequence range, and a capped conversion price if they convert to a 12-month commitment. Procurement wants the conversion price capped in the MAP.

Proposed commercial fallback I can offer without legal review:
- Pilot: 3 months Premium Support at current committed run-rate + one-time pilot fee waived; includes 2-week scheduled spike window.
- Conversion: capped uplift at +15% over current committed run-rate if signed within 30 days of pilot end; 10% onboarding credit applied month 1.
- SLO credits: sliding monthly credit up to 15% of monthly invoice if SLO missed more than 2 separate rolling windows in a quarter (detailed in SLA addendum).

Ben — do these concession levels look ok to approve for signature? If not, please advise max discount / credit we can offer.

—Connor
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Alicia Turner <alicia@kestrel.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel renewal capacity + SLA conversation

Connor / team —

I'm comfortable with the commercial fallback you outlined with a small tweak: convert price cap of +12% (not 15%) if they execute within 30 days post-pilot. We can allow up to 15% SLO credit in the rare event of systemic miss (as long as engineering signs off).

We should include one additional operational guardrail: a joint post-pilot runbook sign-off and a single rollback day option (customer can request a rollback to previous routing if production regressions surface during first 30 days after conversion).

I'll authorize Connor to send a revised SLA addendum and MAP reflecting the cap at +12% and the rollback clause. Laura — please prepare the ops checklist & acceptance criteria.

Thanks —Ben
From: Alicia Turner <alicia@kestrel.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel renewal capacity + SLA conversation

All — great, that aligns with what procurement will accept. Two quick items before I route to legal/procurement:

1) Please add explicit language in the SLA addendum that the 99.9th percentile SLO applies to sequences up to 1k tokens and that longer sequences are excluded (but we agree to a separate performance review).
2) Add the capped conversion price at +12% and the rollback day to the MAP.

If you can send the DocuSign bundle with the SLA addendum + MAP today we will route to procurement and legal for signature. Alicia (procurement) will be the signer for Kestrel.

Appreciate the flexibility — looking forward to getting this over the line.

—Alicia Turner
Head of Platform, Kestrel AI
